lines.cold: [low, measured] Pine Hollow, Montana. Population eleven hundred and change. [unhurried] Saturday night was the Harvest Festival. Lanterns strung all along the north field, where the lake path starts into the pines. [somber] Clara Hale, thirty-four, was seen at that festival a little after nine. By seven the next morning, her Subaru was sitting at the Copper Lake trailhead. Keys in the ignition. Her phone, gone. [pause] Clara, gone.
lines.h1: [steady] You must be the one Helena sent. Sam Ortiz, state police.
lines.h2: [matter-of-fact] Clara Hale. Thirty-four. Owns the bakery on Main Street. Last seen at the Harvest Festival, Saturday, a little after nine.
lines.h3: [somber] Her car turned up at the Copper Lake trailhead Sunday morning. Keys in it. Phone gone. Three days now.
lines.h4: [even] I've done the interviews. Everything I have is in this folder.
lines.h5: [firm] These three envelopes stay sealed. Each one opens when you crack a piece of this. Not before.
lines.h6: [probing] First question. Where did Clara go Saturday night, and did she drive there herself?
lines.h7: [steady] Start with the folder. Take out what you need. I'll check in.
lines.obj1_wrong: [skeptical] Then explain the voicemail. Nine-twelve, she's on the lake path, on foot, out of breath. Listen to her again.
lines.aha: [quiet, impressed] Whoever drove her car to that trailhead needed it that way to reach the pedals.
lines.push_who: [patient] Daniel's boot print is from four o'clock. He's six-three. Look at that seat again.
lines.push_why: [even] Listen to what Clara told Ruth at nine-twelve. Money. Not the house.
lines.push_how: [probing] Somebody mentioned the rocks by the boathouse before anyone told them. Who?
lines.push_drove: [dry] Clara is five-ten. Whoever drove that car needed the seat all the way up.
lines.push_proof: [flat] Your evidence does not prove it. Pick the things that put Marcy on that path.
lines.sol1: [low, measured] Clara found out her partner had been skimming from the bakery. The September and October ledger pages were torn out.
lines.sol2: [steady] At the festival, Clara told Marcy she was going to the sheriff on Monday. You'll ruin me. That is what the pastor heard.
lines.sol3: [quiet] Clara took a lantern from booth fourteen and walked up the lake path. Marcy followed her.
lines.sol4: [somber] They argued. Marcy shoved her. Clara hit her head on the rocks by the old boathouse. Marcy panicked, hid her, took the phone, and drove the Subaru to the trailhead with the seat jammed all the way forward.
lines.sol5: [measured] Then she walked back into town along Route 9 at ten-forty, right past a gas station camera. On Monday, Clara's phone came back on two blocks from Juniper Lane, where Marcy lives.
lines.found: [somber, quiet] Clara Hale was found in the old boathouse on Copper Lake. Ruth Kessler and Clara's family have been told.
lines.softfail: [tired, kind] I made the arrest. You got close. Here's what tipped it.
lines.welcome: [warm, dry] Welcome back. Your desk is just how you left it.
